description:
As many of you may know there is a multiplayer mod being worked on for Star Sector, SSMP Star Sector Multiplayer. Its made significant progress and there is more available than this branch but this was a stable one that is being uploaded for public testing and is stable up to 10 players (47 confirmed in a private test)

I am hosting a competition of User submitted videos to upload to youtube for the 1.0 Release.

Prizes will be awarded to the 3 Top Rated videos, Third place gets 15$ Second place gets 25$, and First place gets their video made as the official SSMP 1.0 Release Trailer + 100$. (Im comfortable with most payment methods, apple pay, cashapp, venmo, paypal, and if its something i dont have and its decent to setup ill try to use your preferred method. (1 upload per person, everyone in a video can submit videos though)

These videos should include Gameplay footage, Highlights, hopefully funny moments with friends, Intense battles, Trading, (current bug abuse is fine too), and anything you think would look good for a 1.0 Release Trailer for youtube. Anyone can submit but the official youtube video can only be something that resembles a genuine trailer/gameplay footage showcasing a mod.
If simple funny video compellation gets the most votes but it doesn't resemble either a trailer or full gameplay showcase, they will receive the 100$ reward but the next video that has trailer potential will get the youtube video uploaded. (Subject to change if many people disagree)

Source code is available and if anyone has Genuine questions please reply here for questions on the code, bugs, launching issues etc...

You do NOT need to download the source to inspect it, every time the build is updated, the main source on the initial page is updated too, you might have to click ---SSMP- To get to that page.

Discord is on the GitHub Join for bug reports updates quick responses from me or general questions + feature request.
Also feel free to ask questions about the code or let me know if genuine issues here. If i take more than 12 hours to respond feel free to ping or DM me on discord @ blazingblazed

Download Here
https://github.com/blazingblazed1/Star-Sector-Multiplayer---SSMP-/releases/tag/SSMP-0.9.4.4
Download Here

https://youtu.be/TBNGdgFlMjk Showcase of this mod version (this is not the latest build but the latest public build...)

Please don't judge this build too harshly, it has been a while in the making and the last thing I wanted to do was drop a "slop" mod which is why no one heard about this mod up and till about 2 weeks ago after all the early builds were fixed up. This mod is NOT the final version and if it takes longer to get this mod right, release date will be pushed back, but progress seems good and a full 1.0 Release seems doable by Next friday (Oct - 30th)

For Videos please make your own forum post and reply with the link here in this comment section. Original forum post likes will be the qualifier for who makes it in first, second, and third place in this contest. Reply with your link here and spread your forum page around to ensure people can judge your videos accordingly.

This was confirmed by alex before posting but i will send this to him hopefully he can dm me or reply here with any changes

Features List
Here is the full feature list. Bug fixes are left out, and I've marked the features that are new in 0.9.4.x.

Connection and setup
- Online play over Iroh peer-to-peer with a join code, so no port forwarding or VPN is needed.
- LAN mode: local network only, with automatic game discovery and no join codes, and it works through a VPN such as Hamachi. The Hamachi case is untested. (New in 0.9.3.9.)
- 2–10 players. It has been tested live with 4.
- A replacement main menu with Single Player, Multiplayer, Options and Quit.
- A lobby with ready checks, version and mod mismatch flags, and ping display.
- The host's newest save is sent to everyone, and the join code stays the same between sessions.
- Reconnecting from inside the game (F8).
- Windows and Linux installers, including a fully static Linux helper that also runs on NixOS.
- An optional "Starsector (SSMP)" launcher with Iroh and LAN modes.
- Background windows keep running while unfocused, at a capped frame rate.
- Test tooling: a multibox script that makes extra game copies for testing, and a bot load-test script.
- Diagnostics, in tester builds only: crash reports, F9 bug reports and an F10 performance overlay.

Shared world
- One shared world run by the host. It keeps running while the host is in menus, dialogs or markets ("Never pause").
- Pause and fast-forward are shared. Guests follow the host's pause, date and fast-forward speed.
- Shared NPC fleets: the host's fleets are the real ones, and guests see them as live copies. Fleets destroyed by anyone are gone for everyone. Hostile fleets can chase any player, and fleets hold still while anyone is talking to or fighting them.
- Faster hyperspace travel while playing together (default ×1.5).
- Shared markets, including storage. Each extra player adds 40% more stock at restock. A purchase someone else got first is refunded.
- Each player has their own fleet, character, skills, officers, reputation, commission, missions and position. These are saved under your player name, so rejoining with the same name restores them.
- New players start fresh with a choice of the five vanilla starts.
- Autosave when a player leaves and every 15 minutes.
- Hyperspace, system and map markers for other players (blue P).

Social and interface
- Scoreboard (~) (tilde below esc): contact any player from anywhere, change your name once every 5 minutes, and pick any portrait.
- Click another player's fleet to contact them.
- Text chat on the campaign map and in battles: movable, resizable and scrollable, with a switch to turn it off.
- Map pings (middle-click) on the map and in battles, with filters per layer.
- Intel entries and notices for players' battles and trades.
- Player list in Intel and on the Factions screen: other players and alliances appear there. (New in 0.9.4.0.)
- Your toolbar, map filters, zoom and refit filters are kept per character.

Economy and trading
- Player-to-player trade: cargo, ships and credits, with a check mark and countdown. Officers stay with their owner, and you can't trade your flagship.
- Out-of-system tax: sending credits costs the sender 100% extra, and items and ships cost 50%. It's free in the same system.
- Shared loot from battles, split half by damage dealt and half by damage taken. All players can participate and gain based on their contribution. If one player takes 100% of all damage that was received by players, their minimum reward is 50% of the total loot of that battle.
- Reputation is applied equally to everyone in a fight.
- Fleets near a friendly or neutral, planet or station no longer use supplies to prevent afk players from getting their storage used up.

Alliances and PvP
- Alliances, with an Alliance tab in the Intel screen.
- Alliance storage at Military Base and High Command markets.
- PvP, which the host can switch on, with a protection period for players already in the campaign.

Co-op combat
- Join another player's battle. You command only your own ships, and losses apply to your own fleet.
- Other players' ships fight on your side (blue) and cannot be commanded by you.
- Your own ships keep their exact loadouts, weapon groups, officers and CR.
- Joiners can fly their flagship, and use their own key bindings, target lock, vent, shield and weapon groups.
- Orders from the tactical map apply to your own ships.
- Joiners' turrets aim at their mouse.
- Guests can deploy only the combat ships they pick
- Joining a fight already in progress ("hot-join").

Host control
- Host settings: max players, and who can pause, fast-forward or kick (everyone, host plus admins, or host only).
- Votes for anything you don't have permission for: pause or fast-forward, with more than half yes within 20 seconds.
- Kick and admin management.
- Switches for map pings, never-pause, shared NPCs and hyperspace speed.

Bug Reporting
- F9 Generates a bug report of everything that happened in the past 6 minutes and it records everything including all visable fleets on screen player actions etc... Will help diagnose sync issues Filepath is mods/playerlogs/(your username ingame)/ txt files

Crash Log
- Automatically depositing a log in your mods/crashlogs folder in your games directory. This file is auto deleted if your game is shutdown normally, if you alt+f4, or Force close with task manager, or your game crashes, there is nothing to delete this log so if any issues occur during loading or during your game, you can self diagnose or post in the SSMP Discord in a private thread for me to take a look at. This log updates every 100 ms with a maximum recording time of 45 seconds to reduce file size, besides anything more than 30 seconds before a crash is mostly useless anyways.

How it Works

1. Game start
Everyone runs Starsector normally with the StarMP mod enabled. The mod starts a small
helper program, smnet, written in Rust. The helper handles the network, and the mod
talks to it, so the game itself never touches a socket.

2. Connecting
The host clicks Host and gets a join code. Friends paste it to join. Online play uses
Iroh, which builds an encrypted peer-to-peer QUIC connection, so no port forwarding or
VPN is needed. In LAN mode Iroh isn't used at all: the host opens a plain TCP port and
games on the local network (or a VPN like Hamachi) show up in a list on the Join screen.

3. Host and guests
The network is a star. Guests talk only to the host, and the host talks to everyone.
Guests never connect to each other. Anything one guest sends another goes through the
host. This keeps one player in charge of the truth and keeps the design simple.

4. Packets
Everything is a small binary packet: a type byte followed by data. Positions, fleet
commands, trades, chat, battle results, settings, votes and pings each have their own
type. The connection only carries them. The helper reconnects and passes them between
the helper and the game.

5. Lobby
Players pick a name, see who is connected, and check ready. The lobby flags anyone
whose mod version or enabled mods differ from the host's, because mismatches cause
crashes. The host decides who may pause, fast-forward or kick, the player limit, and
whether the world pauses or keeps running while menus are open.

6. World and saves
The host's save is the world. When the campaign starts, the host's newest save is sent
to every player once, and everyone loads it. Each player's own fleet, cargo, officers,
skills, reputation and position are stored in the host's save under their name, so
rejoining with the same name brings it all back. New players pick one of the five
vanilla starts. The host autosaves when someone leaves and every 15 minutes.

7. Campaign sync
Each player flies their own fleet. Players regularly send their position, speed and
fleet to the host, and the host sends everyone the others. Time and orbits follow the
host: guests follow the host's date, pause and fast-forward, and planet positions are
corrected from the host so everyone sees the same sky.
NPC fleets are the host's. The host sends fleets near a player and each guest shows
them as live copies, while the guest's own local copies of those fleets are removed.
This stops invisible local fleets from scanning or ambushing you. A fleet one player
destroys is gone for everyone. Where the host isn't present, or during the tutorial,
a guest simply plays its own local world.
Markets, storage and stock are the host's. Missions and bounties stay personal.

8. Trading and economy
Players trade cargo, ships and credits with a ready check and a short countdown.
Sending across systems costs extra, which keeps distance meaningful. Alliances, shared
alliance storage, a scoreboard, chat and map pings are layered on top of the same packets.

9. Combat
Whoever starts a battle runs it and becomes the authority. Nearby players are offered
the chance to join with their own ships and pick which to deploy. Their ships are
rebuilt on the battle owner's game with exact loadouts, officers and combat readiness.
Joiners send only their inputs: keys, mouse, weapon groups, shields and targets. The
owner simulates everything and sends back ship states, shots and missiles. Joiners
steer their own flagship and give orders to their own ships from the tactical map.
When the battle ends, losses, damage, loot and reputation are applied to each fleet.
Loot is split by damage dealt and damage taken.

10. Smoothing and reliability
Between packets, each screen predicts motion from the last known position and speed,
then corrects when the next update arrives. Online traffic travels over reliable QUIC
streams, so lost packets are resent automatically. Diagnostics builds record detailed
reports with F9, which helps find desync and crash causes.

Everything above is checked on multi-game test rigs before release. If you want me to
go deeper on any step, ask.

AI Use Disclaimer
To clarify: SSMP is built with heavy AI assistance.

It started as a hand-built multiplayer framework made for other games, including FATE.
Early SSMP versions were hand-coded, up to the first working lobby connection.

AI use began about 2 months ago, as the tools became capable enough.
Claude writes and debugs the Java mod and the Rust network helper, builds it, and tests it.
ChatGPT helped with UI changes and the main menu.

I direct the project, choose every feature, and playtest every build with the community.
Nothing is released that hasn't been run on my pc, Many VM's have been tested to ensure that no files on fresh OS installs are left behind, nothing else running on your pc after running this program. The biggest concern is smnet and its been tested to ensure that it closes properly when your game closes.

The source is public on GitHub, and the full source ships with each release.
There is no anti-cheat. Only play with people you trust or add screen sharing to public calls.

If someone considers this a dealbreaker, I'm happy to hand over the early hand-coded versions.
Whoever the original community picks in a vote will run the project.
Votes count only original members, not people who joined shortly before.

Many people have claimed I "denied ai use" I dont believe i ever have. Some people early on asked if it was all ai coded, and my usual reply was I dont believe anyone can just tell an ai to "Make a star sector mod" and get something similar to this. I was harassed for this before and this is why i will no longer be doing public Q&A in USC or Corvus. Those people were not wanting genuine answers they just wanted to troll and im trying to keep everything from here on out respectful. Replys to this forum post or in my discord located in the GitHub is where i will reply.

Frequently Asked Questions
SSMP (StarMP) - FAQ

What is SSMP?
A co-op multiplayer mod for Starsector 0.98a-RC8. Each player flies their own fleet in a shared campaign. Drag-and-drop install, no extra downloads.

Why does the one-click launcher create a desktop icon?
That icon lets you choose how to launch: with Iroh (the integrated VPN, for internet play) or LAN (so players can use a VPN of their own choice). A plain drag-and-drop of the mod folder still works fine too, just enable SSMP and disable other mods to prevent conflicts.

How do I install it?
Unzip the StarMP folder into Starsector\mods, enable it in the launcher. Everyone needs the same SSMP version. If Windows Firewall asks about the network helper, allow it.

How many players?
Up to 10 in a lobby. Tested heavily with 6-8 people, and benchmarking with up to 47 clients on the same server.

Is it safe to run? It's AI-assisted.
AI-assisted doesn't mean unverified. The full source is public, the networking code is open, and the code has been reviewed by other people in the modding community. "Made with AI" is about how it was built, not what it does, and what it does is all readable.

Does the mod read my Windows registry?
No, the mod's own code never touches the registry. The networking library (Iroh) reads your DNS-server list from it, read-only, so it can resolve the server address and connect, the exact same thing Steam, Discord, and your browser do every time they go online. It doesn't read anything personal: no SID, no hardware ID, no installed programs, and it writes nothing. The specific dependencies are windows-registry and ipconfig, pulled in by Iroh's DNS resolver, verifiable in the Cargo.lock.

Is SSMP more invasive than other apps?
No, it's less. It runs as a normal user process: no kernel driver, no background service, no autostart, no registry writes. Discord reads your running-process list; Steam runs a service and writes to the registry; Valorant's anti-cheat runs a kernel driver at boot. SSMP reads your DNS config to connect and nothing else.

What is Iroh / what gets sent?
Iroh is an open-source peer-to-peer networking library that handles connections without you needing a VPN or port forwarding. Only game state flows over it, fleet positions, trades, battle data. It's not a modified copy: it's pulled from the official Rust package registry and pinned by checksum, so anyone can confirm it's the unmodified original.

Can I verify the code myself?
Yes. The source is public, the Iroh version is checksum-pinned to the official release, and release builds are reproducible, you can compile from source and confirm the binary matches, nothing added.

Is there anti-cheat?
No. Every player's game is trusted, so anyone in your session can affect your fleet, credits, and save. Only play with people you trust.

Can I play over LAN instead of the internet?
Yes, the launcher lets you pick IROH (internet) or LAN. LAN runs with no external networking binary, ideal if you're on the same network or bringing your own VPN.

Does it work with other mods?
No official mod support yet. Technically, any mod that doesn't affect AI fleets or generation should be fine  as long as every player has the exact same mods.

What platforms?
Windows and Linux. No macOS build of the network helper yet. Working on MAC Support but have not had enough mac testers to get the build working.

How do I host or join?
Host: Multiplayer -> Host Game -> copy the join code, send it to friends. Friends: Join Game (code pastes automatically) -> Join. Everyone hits Ready, host hits Start, the host's save copies to everyone.

Found a bug — what do I do?
Report it with your logs: saves\common\starmp_log.txt.data and starsector-core\starsector.log. Say whether you were host or guest and what happened just before. Please join the offical SSMP Discord on the GitHub and create a private thread, only you and me can see it there.

Will this corrupt my save?
Back up your saves, it's an early test release. The host's save is the shared world; guests load a copy.

"JOIN BATTLE" option in a player's contact dialog.

Vanilla tutorial now runs locally for each player.

Crash report keeps the last 45 seconds before a crash (was 30).

Large battles: ship definitions are sent only for new ships, roughly halving the host's upload in 100+ ship fights.

- Diagnostics, in tester builds only: crash reports, F9 bug reports and an F10 performance overlay.

Shared world
- One shared world run by the host. It keeps running while the host is in menus, dialogs or markets ("Never pause").
- Pause and fast-forward are shared. Guests follow the host's pause, date and fast-forward speed.
- Shared NPC fleets: the host's fleets are the real ones, and guests see them as live copies. Fleets destroyed by anyone are gone for everyone. Hostile fleets can chase any player, and fleets hold still while anyone is talking to or fighting them.
- Faster hyperspace travel while playing together (default ×1.5).
- Shared markets, including storage. Each extra player adds 40% more stock at restock. A purchase someone else got first is refunded.
- Each player has their own fleet, character, skills, officers, reputation, commission, missions and position. These are saved under your player name, so rejoining with the same name restores them.
- New players start fresh with a choice of the five vanilla starts.
- Autosave when a player leaves and every 15 minutes.
- Hyperspace, system and map markers for other players (blue P).

Social and interface
- Scoreboard (~) (tilde below esc): contact any player from anywhere, change your name once every 5 minutes, and pick any portrait.
- Click another player's fleet to contact them.
- Text chat on the campaign map and in battles: movable, resizable and scrollable, with a switch to turn it off.
- Map pings (middle-click) on the map and in battles, with filters per layer.
- Intel entries and notices for players' battles and trades.
- Player list in Intel and on the Factions screen: other players and alliances appear there. (New in 0.9.4.0.)
- Your toolbar, map filters, zoom and refit filters are kept per character.

Economy and trading
- Player-to-player trade: cargo, ships and credits, with a check mark and countdown. Officers stay with their owner, and you can't trade your flagship.
- Out-of-system tax: sending credits costs the sender 100% extra, and items and ships cost 50%. It's free in the same system.
- Shared loot from battles, split half by damage dealt and half by damage taken. All players can participate and gain based on their contribution. If one player takes 100% of all damage that was received by players, their minimum reward is 50% of the total loot of that battle.
- Reputation is applied equally to everyone in a fight.
- Fleets near a friendly or neutral, planet or station no longer use supplies to prevent afk players from getting their storage used up.

Alliances and PvP
- Alliances, with an Alliance tab in the Intel screen.
- Alliance storage at Military Base and High Command markets.
- PvP, which the host can switch on, with a protection period for players already in the campaign.

Co-op combat
- Join another player's battle. You command only your own ships, and losses apply to your own fleet.
- Other players' ships fight on your side (blue) and cannot be commanded by you.
- Your own ships keep their exact loadouts, weapon groups, officers and CR.
- Joiners can fly their flagship, and use their own key bindings, target lock, vent, shield and weapon groups.
- Orders from the tactical map apply to your own ships.
- Joiners' turrets aim at their mouse.
- Guests can deploy only the combat ships they pick
- Joining a fight already in progress ("hot-join").

Host control
- Host settings: max players, and who can pause, fast-forward or kick (everyone, host plus admins, or host only).
- Votes for anything you don't have permission for: pause or fast-forward, with more than half yes within 20 seconds.
- Kick and admin management.
- Switches for map pings, never-pause, shared NPCs and hyperspace speed.

Bug Reporting
- F9 Generates a bug report of everything that happened in the past 6 minutes and it records everything including all visable fleets on screen player actions etc... Will help diagnose sync issues Filepath is mods/playerlogs/(your username ingame)/ txt files

Crash Log
- Automatically depositing a log in your mods/crashlogs folder in your games directory. This file is auto deleted if your game is shutdown normally, if you alt+f4, or Force close with task manager, or your game crashes, there is nothing to delete this log so if any issues occur during loading or during your game, you can self diagnose or post in the SSMP Discord in a private thread for me to take a look at. This log updates every 100 ms with a maximum recording time of 45 seconds to reduce file size, besides anything more than 30 seconds before a crash is mostly useless anyways.

How it Works

1. Game start
Everyone runs Starsector normally with the StarMP mod enabled. The mod starts a small
helper program, smnet, written in Rust. The helper handles the network, and the mod
talks to it, so the game itself never touches a socket.

2. Connecting
The host clicks Host and gets a join code. Friends paste it to join. Online play uses
Iroh, which builds an encrypted peer-to-peer QUIC connection, so no port forwarding or
VPN is needed. In LAN mode Iroh isn't used at all: the host opens a plain TCP port and
games on the local network (or a VPN like Hamachi) show up in a list on the Join screen.

3. Host and guests
The network is a star. Guests talk only to the host, and the host talks to everyone.
Guests never connect to each other. Anything one guest sends another goes through the
host. This keeps one player in charge of the truth and keeps the design simple.

4. Packets
Everything is a small binary packet: a type byte followed by data. Positions, fleet
commands, trades, chat, battle results, settings, votes and pings each have their own
type. The connection only carries them. The helper reconnects and passes them between
the helper and the game.

5. Lobby
Players pick a name, see who is connected, and check ready. The lobby flags anyone
whose mod version or enabled mods differ from the host's, because mismatches cause
crashes. The host decides who may pause, fast-forward or kick, the player limit, and
whether the world pauses or keeps running while menus are open.

6. World and saves
The host's save is the world. When the campaign starts, the host's newest save is sent
to every player once, and everyone loads it. Each player's own fleet, cargo, officers,
skills, reputation and position are stored in the host's save under their name, so
rejoining with the same name brings it all back. New players pick one of the five
vanilla starts. The host autosaves when someone leaves and every 15 minutes.

7. Campaign sync
Each player flies their own fleet. Players regularly send their position, speed and
fleet to the host, and the host sends everyone the others. Time and orbits follow the
host: guests follow the host's date, pause and fast-forward, and planet positions are
corrected from the host so everyone sees the same sky.
NPC fleets are the host's. The host sends fleets near a player and each guest shows
them as live copies, while the guest's own local copies of those fleets are removed.
This stops invisible local fleets from scanning or ambushing you. A fleet one player
destroys is gone for everyone. Where the host isn't present, or during the tutorial,
a guest simply plays its own local world.
Markets, storage and stock are the host's. Missions and bounties stay personal.

8. Trading and economy
Players trade cargo, ships and credits with a ready check and a short countdown.
Sending across systems costs extra, which keeps distance meaningful. Alliances, shared
alliance storage, a scoreboard, chat and map pings are layered on top of the same packets.

9. Combat
Whoever starts a battle runs it and becomes the authority. Nearby players are offered
the chance to join with their own ships and pick which to deploy. Their ships are
rebuilt on the battle owner's game with exact loadouts, officers and combat readiness.
Joiners send only their inputs: keys, mouse, weapon groups, shields and targets. The
owner simulates everything and sends back ship states, shots and missiles. Joiners
steer their own flagship and give orders to their own ships from the tactical map.
When the battle ends, losses, damage, loot and reputation are applied to each fleet.
Loot is split by damage dealt and damage taken.

10. Smoothing and reliability
Between packets, each screen predicts motion from the last known position and speed,
then corrects when the next update arrives. Online traffic travels over reliable QUIC
streams, so lost packets are resent automatically. Diagnostics builds record detailed
reports with F9, which helps find desync and crash causes.

Everything above is checked on multi-game test rigs before release. If you want me to
go deeper on any step, ask.

Frequently Asked Questions
SSMP (StarMP) - FAQ

What is SSMP?
A co-op multiplayer mod for Starsector 0.98a-RC8. Each player flies their own fleet in a shared campaign. Drag-and-drop install, no extra downloads.

Why does the one-click launcher create a desktop icon?
That icon lets you choose how to launch: with Iroh (the integrated VPN, for internet play) or LAN (so players can use a VPN of their own choice). A plain drag-and-drop of the mod folder still works fine too, just enable SSMP and disable other mods to prevent conflicts.

How do I install it?
Unzip the StarMP folder into Starsector\mods, enable it in the launcher. Everyone needs the same SSMP version. If Windows Firewall asks about the network helper, allow it.

How many players?
Up to 10 in a lobby. Tested heavily with 6-8 people, and benchmarking with up to 47 clients on the same server.

Is it safe to run? It's AI-assisted.
AI-assisted doesn't mean unverified. The full source is public, the networking code is open, and the code has been reviewed by other people in the modding community. "Made with AI" is about how it was built, not what it does, and what it does is all readable.

Does the mod read my Windows registry?
No, the mod's own code never touches the registry. The networking library (Iroh) reads your DNS-server list from it, read-only, so it can resolve the server address and connect, the exact same thing Steam, Discord, and your browser do every time they go online. It doesn't read anything personal: no SID, no hardware ID, no installed programs, and it writes nothing. The specific dependencies are windows-registry and ipconfig, pulled in by Iroh's DNS resolver, verifiable in the Cargo.lock.

Is SSMP more invasive than other apps?
No, it's less. It runs as a normal user process: no kernel driver, no background service, no autostart, no registry writes. Discord reads your running-process list; Steam runs a service and writes to the registry; Valorant's anti-cheat runs a kernel driver at boot. SSMP reads your DNS config to connect and nothing else.

What is Iroh / what gets sent?
Iroh is an open-source peer-to-peer networking library that handles connections without you needing a VPN or port forwarding. Only game state flows over it, fleet positions, trades, battle data. It's not a modified copy: it's pulled from the official Rust package registry and pinned by checksum, so anyone can confirm it's the unmodified original.

Can I verify the code myself?
Yes. The source is public, the Iroh version is checksum-pinned to the official release, and release builds are reproducible, you can compile from source and confirm the binary matches, nothing added.

Is there anti-cheat?
No. Every player's game is trusted, so anyone in your session can affect your fleet, credits, and save. Only play with people you trust.

Can I play over LAN instead of the internet?
Yes, the launcher lets you pick IROH (internet) or LAN. LAN runs with no external networking binary, ideal if you're on the same network or bringing your own VPN.

Does it work with other mods?
No official mod support yet. Technically, any mod that doesn't affect AI fleets or generation should be fine  as long as every player has the exact same mods.

What platforms?
Windows and Linux. No macOS build of the network helper yet. Working on MAC Support but have not had enough mac testers to get the build working.

How do I host or join?
Host: Multiplayer -> Host Game -> copy the join code, send it to friends. Friends: Join Game (code pastes automatically) -> Join. Everyone hits Ready, host hits Start, the host's save copies to everyone.

Found a bug — what do I do?
Report it with your logs: saves\common\starmp_log.txt.data and starsector-core\starsector.log. Say whether you were host or guest and what happened just before. Please join the offical SSMP Discord on the GitHub and create a private thread, only you and me can see it there.

Will this corrupt my save?
Back up your saves, it's an early test release. The host's save is the shared world; guests load a copy.
